title: Edit Distance
seoDescription: Compute Levenshtein distance as the minimum insertions, deletions, and substitutions needed to transform one string into another.
description:
Compute minimum single-character edit operations (insertion, deletion, substitution) transforming string s1 into string s2.

$$
D(i, j) = \begin{cases} D(i-1, j-1) & \text{if } s_1[i] = s_2[j] \\ 1 + \min(D(i-1, j), D(i, j-1), D(i-1, j-1)) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$

Given input parameters `s1`, `s2`, return integer representing minimum edit operations.

### 💡 Intuition & Approach
**Edit Distance** (NLP, Data Processing): Compute Levenshtein distance as the minimum insertions, deletions, and substitutions needed to transform one string into another.

To implement `nlp_edit_distance` cleanly and accurately:
1. Parse and normalize the inputs (`s1`, `s2`) into floating-point arrays or structured containers.
2. Execute the mathematical transformation defined in the problem specification while guarding denominators and boundary conditions.
3. Round floating-point outputs to the target precision and return the expected `int` structure.

### ⚡ Python Reference Implementation
```python
def nlp_edit_distance(s1: str, s2: str) -> int:
    m, n = len(s1), len(s2)
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]
    for i in range(m + 1): dp[i][0] = i
    for j in range(n + 1): dp[0][j] = j
    for i in range(1, m + 1):
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if s1[i-1] == s2[j-1] else 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])
    return dp[m][n]
```
